social_circle_metadata.note: John is a 2-year-old and does not own a phone. The five contacts below are the people whose personal text correspondence with the Garrity household is centered on John — i.e., John's effective text-message social circle, mediated through his mother Sarah's and father Mark's personal phones (SMS, iMessage, and the private family WhatsApp group described in Q48).

social_circle.name: Linda Bennett ("Gramma Linda")

background.how_they_met: John's grandmother by birth — Sarah's mother. Linda flew in from Spokane and stayed in the Olympia Street guest room for the entire first month after John was born in March 2024, and has been a near-daily presence in his life since.
background.why_close: Linda is the most emotionally invested extended-family member in John's day-to-day life. She FaceTimes him every other day from Spokane, stays in the guest room one long week each quarter, and was Sarah's primary postpartum support. Sarah is also Linda's closest emotional outlet, so a large share of texts between them concern John's milestones, naps, and small dramas.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in long, fully-punctuated sentences with one exclamation per message. Sends photos of cardinals at her bird feeder. Frequent voice notes addressed to John ("Hi sweetheart, it's Gramma!"). Uses heart and sunshine emojis but never slang. Has been managing low-grade depression with antidepressants for a decade (Q46), and the texting tone reflects gentle, slightly worry-prone warmth.

shared_activities: FaceTime story-reading sessions (Goodnight Moon and Eric Carle picture books)
Quarterly week-long visits in the Olympia Street guest room
Christmas, Easter, and the Lake Coeur d'Alene summer cabin weekend
Sending John knitted things and small books in the mail
social_circle.communication_frequency: daily (FaceTime every other day with text photos and voice notes on the alternating days)
recent_text_topics: Asking for updates after John's January 2026 ear infection and the amoxicillin course; Linda still checks in periodically about his ears.
Coordinating Linda's upcoming summer cabin weekend at Lake Coeur d'Alene and what John can eat there (she remembers he refuses peas).
Sending iPhone photos of cardinals at the Spokane bird feeder for John to point at on Sarah's phone.
Quiet sister-level support to Sarah about her February 2026 Kennewick School District board meeting — Linda was proud of her for going.
Anxiety-tinged check-ins about wildfire smoke forecasts as summer approaches and whether the HEPA filter in John's bedroom is still working.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05: 'he calls her "Gramma Linda" — she FaceTimes him almost every other day from Spokane and he absolutely lights up.' Q04: 'My mom flew in from Spokane for the first month after John was born.' Q11/Q13: 'my mom stays in the guest room when she visits, usually one long week per quarter.' Q46: maternal grandmother's long-term antidepressant use.

social_circle.name: Rachel Sutton

background.how_they_met: Sarah's older sister; John's aunt and the mother of his cousin Mia (age 4). The two sister households have been in close contact since John was born, alternating drives between Kennewick and Spokane every other month.
background.why_close: Rachel is Sarah's go-to sibling for parenting comparisons — Mia is two years ahead of John, so Rachel has already lived through every milestone Sarah is currently navigating. The cousins overlap at Christmas, Easter, July 4th, and the Lake Coeur d'Alene cabin weekend, and Rachel is John's most plugged-in extended-family adult after Gramma Linda.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in short, efficient lines, often back-to-back. Drops in OT-specific suggestions ("try the heavy-work blocks before nap") unprompted. Uses one or two emojis per thread. Forwards Instagram reels of Mia bossing other kids around. Was the family member who went to a BLM march in Spokane (Q30), and is the more politically vocal aunt — but keeps that out of texts about John.

shared_activities: Alternating Kennewick-Spokane visits every other month with the cousins
Christmas, Easter, and July 4th family gatherings
Lake Coeur d'Alene summer cabin weekend
Sharing hand-me-down toddler clothes and Mia's outgrown toys
recent_text_topics: Coordinating the next Spokane-to-Kennewick drive and whether Mia will bring the bossy-princess phase down with her.
Rachel sending OT-flavored advice about John dropping the morning nap in March 2026 — she anticipated the rough week.
Comparing notes on T-ball Saturdays: Mia did 'Tiny Sluggers' last year and Rachel is cracking up about John running to second base because Mark cheers there.
Quietly checking in on Sarah after the February school board meeting and whether the curriculum debate is going anywhere.
Logistics for the Lake Coeur d'Alene cabin weekend in July — who's bringing the inflatable splash pool.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q05: 'one cousin, Mia, who's four — she's my sister Rachel's daughter, also in Spokane... About every other month. We drive up to Spokane or they come down. They overlap at Christmas, Easter, July 4th, and a summer cabin weekend at Lake Coeur d'Alene.' Q30: 'My sister Rachel is more vocal — she went to a march in Spokane.'

social_circle.name: Tim Garrity

background.how_they_met: Mark's younger brother. Has been a regular face in John's life since birth, visiting from Boise alongside Papa and Nana for Thanksgiving, Easter, and John's March birthday.
background.why_close: Tim is John's hands-down favorite uncle (Q06) because he does the 'airplane-spin' game on every visit. He and Mark are tight as adult brothers — they had one heated Thanksgiving over BLM that ended with them turning on football (Q30), and that pattern of strong disagreement plus easy reconciliation defines their bond. John adores him.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short, casual texts. Heavy use of crying-laughing emoji and the occasional GIF. Sends 4-second videos of himself doing dumb voices for John. Avoids politics in family group chats after the Thanksgiving incident.

shared_activities: The airplane-spin game on every visit
Thanksgiving, Easter, and John's birthday in person
Seahawks/college football weekend viewings with Mark
Talking about future fishing trips and the toy tractor collection
recent_text_topics: Asking Mark for video of John's first T-ball Saturday at Southridge in April — wants to see the run-to-second-base bit.
Sending a goofy voice-note as 'Uncle Tim the firetruck' for John (who is deep in his firefighter-helmet phase).
Joking with Mark about how much Sarah's spreadsheet brain has shaped John ("kid lines up shoes by the door, what did you do to him").
Coordinating his next Boise-to-Kennewick visit and whether Papa and Nana are coming too.
Talking minivan recommendations with Mark — Tim has strong HVAC-guy opinions about the Subaru's remaining life.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q06: 'Mark has one brother in Boise too, Uncle Tim... Uncle Tim, no contest — Tim does the airplane-spin game when he visits.' Q05: 'Mark's parents, who he calls "Papa and Nana," and they come down for Thanksgiving and Easter and his birthday.' Q30: 'Mark and Tim had one Thanksgiving where it got heated, then we changed the subject to football.'

social_circle.name: Becky Lawson
social_circle.relationship: close family friend (Sarah's best local friend)

demographics.location: Kennewick, WA (Southridge area, ~10 min from Creekstone)

background.how_they_met: Sarah and Becky met at a Mid-Columbia Library District new-parent storytime when both their kids were ~6 months old, roughly fall 2024. Their toddlers are the same age, which made the friendship stick.
background.why_close: Becky is named in Q49 as one of Sarah's three primary emotional supports (alongside Mark and Linda). The friendship is the textbook same-age-toddler bond: they coordinate playdates almost weekly, swap clothes, and trade real-time texts about whatever stage their kids are in. John sees Becky's toddler often enough to count as a regular playmate alongside Ellie, Marcus, and Lily.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in casual sentences with frequent emojis (especially the laugh-cry and the upside-down face). Sends photos of her kid mid-tantrum captioned 'me too honestly.' Voice notes when she's driving. Heavy meme-forwarder.

shared_activities: Playdates at Lawrence Scott Park and each other's backyards
Tuesday library storytime at the Kennewick Branch with Miss Patty
Costco runs together when schedules align
Splash pad afternoons in summer
recent_text_topics: Negotiating a Lawrence Scott Park playdate around John's afternoon nap schedule now that the morning nap is gone.
Real-time updates during the 'Bee-Bee' missing-blanket crisis in March 2026 — Becky offered her own kid's spare lovey as a decoy (which John rejected).
Comparing notes on Toyota Center pool swim lessons signup for summer 2026.
Forwarding toddler-feeding accounts and laughing about the universal experience of refusing peas.
Venting about wildfire smoke season approaching and trading HEPA-filter model numbers.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q49: 'I lean on Mark, my mom, and one close friend named Becky who has a toddler the same age.' Q48: Sarah follows toddler-feeding accounts on Instagram (shared interest). Q44: described kind of crisis a same-age-toddler friend would naturally be part of.

social_circle.name: Mai Hoang
social_circle.relationship: next-door neighbor (mother of John's regular playmate Lily)

demographics.occupation: Registered nurse, Kadlec Regional Medical Center
demographics.location: Kennewick, WA — Creekstone neighborhood, the house adjoining the Garritys' backyard

background.how_they_met: Mai and her husband moved into the neighboring tan-stucco craftsman in Creekstone around the same time the Garritys did. The two families realized their kids were close in age (Lily is 3, John is 2) and installed the small connecting gate between the two backyards.
background.why_close: Functional best-friend-by-proximity. The shared gate means the kids see each other 3-4 times a week, and the constant playdate logistics make Mai one of the most-texted contacts on Sarah's phone. Mark and Mai's husband are friendly but the day-to-day text channel runs mom-to-mom. The Hoangs are also part of Sarah and Mark's intentional effort to make diversity John's default (Q28).

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Short, friendly, logistics-heavy texts. Uses thumbs-up and plant emoji. Often texts in the format 'kids are out back — coffee?' Sends nurse-level calm replies when Sarah panics about a John bump or rash. Doesn't do voice notes — too many night shifts have made her a typer.

shared_activities: Daily-ish backyard playdates through the shared gate
Trading vegetables from each other's gardens (Hoangs grow Asian greens, the Garritys' herb pots)
July 4th block party on the cul-de-sac
Walking the kids to Lawrence Scott Park together
recent_text_topics: Coordinating which yard the kids will be in each afternoon and who's supervising — the standard 'gate's open, send him over' text.
Mai (as an RN) reassuring Sarah by text during John's January 2026 ear infection that the amoxicillin course was the right call.
Sarah asking Mai about Lily's preschool plans for fall — Lily is aging into a different class at Little Sprouts.
Planning the cul-de-sac 4th of July block party — who's bringing what and whether John will still be terrified of sparklers this year.
Trading recommendations for sun-shade canopies as Tri-Cities summer heat ramps toward 105°F again.
